title: 15.0.7 runtime build fails on armv7l with missing unwinder
body: I'm maintaining a multi-platform binary distribution and my 32-bit Arm build of LLVM 15.0.7 fails while building the runtimes. I reproduced it on a clean machine with a minimal CMake configuration enabling clang, lld, lldb, clang-tools-extra, polly and the compiler-rt, libc++, libc++abi and libunwind runtimes, with per-target runtime directories enabled. The failure contains missing-unwinder references. It is not an out-of-memory failure. I also see GNU ld messages saying `DWARF error: invalid or unhandled FORM value: 0x25`; this clean machine has GNU ld 2.35.2.

symptoms_visible: My clean 32-bit Arm build of the LLVM 15.0.7 runtimes stops with missing-unwinder references.
The same build log also contains `/usr/bin/ld: DWARF error: invalid or unhandled FORM value: 0x25`.
N0.label: N0 armv7l runtime build failure reported

symptoms_visible: With GCC 12 and binutils 2.39 I no longer see the DWARF message, but the 32-bit Arm runtime build still fails.
The linker line says `--unwindlib=none`, but unresolved references to the unwinder remain.
A build from the latest main branch fails with the same runtime error.
N1.label: N1 linker version and main branch checked

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding with a different order in `LLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES`, the 32-bit Arm runtime build still fails.
N2_x.label: N2_x runtime-order attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: After applying the suggested runtime patches and disabling GWP-ASan for `armv7l-unknown-linux-gnueabihf`, the build reaches the fuzzer runtime and fails with `clang-15: error: unknown target triple 'armhf-unknown-linux-gnueabihf'`.
My compiler reports its target as `armv7l-unknown-linux-gnueabihf`, while the generated runtime directories and command line use `armhf-unknown-linux-gnueabihf`.
N3_x.label: N3_x GWP-ASan workaround exposes invalid triple

symptoms_visible: With `LLVM_RUNTIME_TARGETS=armv7l-unknown-linux-gnueabihf`, the invalid `armhf` target error is gone, but linking `libc++abi.so.1.0` fails with `ld: cannot find -lunwind: No such file or directory`.
N4.label: N4 valid runtime triple exposes missing library path

symptoms_visible: After I add the build's `lib` directory to `LDFLAGS`, `libc++abi.so.1.0` finds `libunwind.so` and the LLVM 15 production build completes.
The working script needs the explicit `armv7l-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` runtime target; the other target-specific GWP-ASan definitions are no longer needed.
N5.label: N5 LLVM 15 build passes with local workarounds

symptoms_visible: My normal build scripts complete successfully on x86_64, aarch64 and armv7l with the updated LLVM release.
N_terminal.label: terminal upstream fixes verified

question_patterns: Can you repeat the build with newer binutils, or use DWARF 4, and report separately whether the DWARF warning and missing-unwinder failure remain?
Does the runtime build still fail in your production environment with a newer GNU linker?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My production environment uses GCC 12 and binutils 2.39. I don't see the DWARF error there, but the 32-bit Arm runtime build still fails.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After upgrading binutils, both the DWARF messages and all undefined unwinder references disappear and the runtime build completes.
I tested binutils 2.38 rather than 2.39; the DWARF message is gone but the same missing-unwinder failure remains.

question_patterns: Can you try the same initial configuration against the latest main branch and report whether it gets past the runtime link?
Is this limited to the 15 release, or can you reproduce it with a current source checkout?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I asked for a build with the latest main branch using the same initial configuration, and it failed with the same error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The latest main branch completes with the same configuration; only the 15 release fails.

edges.comment: Messages c1-c3 and c12-c18. The reporter's newer-binutils build separates the unrelated GNU ld DWARF diagnostic from the persistent missing-unwinder failure. The main-branch result was produced for the reporter by a friend and is folded into the same user side as requested by the reporter.

solution.intent: Reorder the entries in LLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES so compiler-rt is built after the C++ and unwind runtimes.
solution.concrete_example: Try changing the order of `LLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES`, moving `compiler-rt` to the end so the other runtime libraries are available first.

edges.comment: Messages c4-c6 on the reporter's armv7l system. The reporter noticed an earlier runtime-order change and rebuilt with a different order, but the failure remained.

solution.intent: Apply the available runtime-build workaround patches and disable GWP-ASan for the exact Arm target to get past the original compiler-rt failure.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the two proposed runtime-build patches, determine the exact target from `clang --version`, and pass `RUNTIMES_armv7l-unknown-linux-gnueabihf_COMPILER_RT_BUILD_GWP_ASAN=OFF`.

edges.comment: Messages c16-c19. Participant2 proposed the temporary patches and target-specific GWP-ASan option; the reporter applied them to the LLVM 15 source and rebuilt. This did not complete the build and instead surfaced the invalid generated armhf triple.

solution.intent: Force the runtimes build to use the compiler's valid armv7l target instead of the generated armhf target.
solution.concrete_example: Configure with `LLVM_RUNTIME_TARGETS=armv7l-unknown-linux-gnueabihf`; alternatively, use the target-scoped default-target-only option so compiler-rt keeps the compiler's target triple unchanged.
solution.inference_hint: Participant2 inspected `get_compiler_rt_target` and determined that an `armhf` architecture value was combined with the suffix of the default `armv7l-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` target, producing the invalid `armhf-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` triple. That code-level conclusion is engineer analysis, not reporter-produced evidence.

edges.comment: Messages c20-c30 on the reporter's build. The explicit runtime target gets past the invalid-triple failure, but it is not sufficient by itself: the build then reaches libc++abi and still cannot locate libunwind.

solution.intent: Use a local LLVM 15 workaround by adding the runtime build's library directory to the linker search path so libc++abi can find libunwind.
solution.concrete_example: Add `-L<build>/lib` to the script's `LDFLAGS`, where the just-built `libunwind.so` is located, and rerun the runtime build.

edges.comment: Messages c32-c34 and c40. The reporter identified that the libc++abi link lacked the path containing the freshly built libunwind, manually added that path to LDFLAGS, and confirmed the LLVM 15 production build passed. This is a successful local workaround, not the upstream CMake repair.

solution.intent: Fix the runtime CMake configuration upstream so dependent runtime links receive the built libunwind search path, while also correcting Arm runtime-target handling, then ask the reporter to verify an updated build with the original scripts.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the upstream runtime-build corrections so libc++abi links against the in-tree libunwind without a manual `LDFLAGS` patch and Arm builds no longer generate the invalid `armhf` target. Please retest with your normal multi-platform build scripts and report whether armv7l completes.
solution.inference_hint: The final accepted diagnosis combines two engineer-maintained CMake defects encountered in the same Arm runtime build: the runtime link did not receive the location of the in-tree libunwind, and compiler-rt's Arm target handling could generate an invalid armhf triple. A separate operator verified the proposed build patch on armv7l before it was merged; the original reporter later performed the terminal verification with the updated release.

edges.comment: Messages c39-c54. Participant4's armv7l setup supplied pre-merge evidence that the runtime patch fixed the build; this is explicitly a different operator's system and is not represented as reporter verification. After the required changes were merged, the original reporter retested their own x86_64, aarch64 and armv7l build scripts and confirmed success.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted missing-unwinder cause: the runtime CMake configuration failed to propagate the directory containing the in-tree libunwind to the libc++abi link; adding that library path made the LLVM 15 build pass.

Must also account for the separate Arm runtime-target defect encountered during diagnosis: per-target handling could transform the valid armv7l target into the invalid armhf target, requiring an explicit valid runtime target as a workaround and an upstream target-handling correction.
Must distinguish the GNU ld DWARF FORM 0x25 diagnostic from the missing-unwinder failure: newer binutils removed the DWARF message but did not fix the runtime build.

Must not present runtime reordering, disabling GWP-ASan, or specifying the valid target triple alone as the complete fix; each was tried or used in-case without independently resolving the missing libunwind link path.

Must ask the reporter to verify the upstream runtime CMake corrections using an updated build before declaring the issue fully resolved; the terminal evidence is the reporter's successful multi-platform build.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced binary-distribution maintainer who writes detailed CMake build scripts, maintains several host architectures, applies source patches, inspects linker command lines and can run long clean production builds, but does not claim deep familiarity with LLVM's internal CMake implementation.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, methodical and cooperative; supplies exact commands and logs, distinguishes hypotheses from confirmed observations, reports long-running build results promptly, and asks focused questions about workaround scope.
